**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of between 250 and 300 words on any one of the following topics. Make sure that you write in paragraphs.

**Topic 1.** Imagine that you are one of the men in Asma Begum's village and you were particularly saddened by the incident. You have been invited to a meeting to advise husbands against violence. In the speech you will deliver, you want to educate the people without antagonising them. Write the speech.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
La rédaction anglaise du BAC sanctionne autant le respect strict du format imposé (discours, article de presse, lettre personnelle) que le contenu : un contenu excellent rédigé dans le mauvais format perd des points que ni les idées ni la grammaire ne peuvent compenser. Un discours s'adresse directement à un auditoire présent (formules d'appel, ton posé et pédagogique plutôt qu'accusateur, puisqu'il s'agit ici de convaincre sans braquer les maris visés) ; un article de presse informe et argumente pour un lectorat qu'on ne connaît pas personnellement, avec un titre et un ton plus démonstratif ; une lettre personnelle (à un ami) respecte les formules d'ouverture et de clôture amicales, un registre plus familier, et peut mêler anecdotes et opinions. Comme le sujet propose un choix entre trois formats, un seul texte doit être rédigé le jour de l'examen ; les trois modèles ci-dessous illustrent chacun l'un des formats possibles.

## Topic 1 - Speech (modèle, environ 270 mots)

Dear friends, dear neighbours,

I did not ask to speak to you today to lecture anyone. I asked to speak because what happened to young Asma Begum in our own community has kept me awake at night, and I believe it should keep every one of us awake too.

A woman was attacked with acid by her own husband, in her sleep, over something as small as a delayed meal. Four other women, who had nothing to do with that quarrel, were burned alongside her. I am not here to shame any particular man among us. I am here because I believe most of us would never imagine doing such a thing, and yet this kind of violence keeps happening in homes we consider ordinary.

Anger is a normal feeling. Every man in this room has felt it towards his wife at some point. The question is not whether we get angry, but what we allow that anger to become. A raised voice fades in a day. A thrown fist leaves a mark for weeks. Acid leaves a mark for life, on her body and on our name as a community.

I am asking each of you, as a friend rather than a judge, to make one simple commitment: the next time anger rises in your home, walk outside before you act. Talk to an elder, a brother, even to me, before that anger becomes something none of us can undo.

Our wives are not our property to punish. They are the mothers of our children and the partners who share our daily struggles. Protecting them is not weakness; it is the mark of a man secure enough in himself not to need violence to be respected.

Let Asma Begum's suffering be the last of its kind in our village, not because the law forced us, but because we chose, together, to be better.

Thank you for listening.

**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of between 250 and 300 words on any one of the following topics. Make sure that you write in paragraphs.

**Topic 2.** You find some of the practices towards women in your village unfair. Write an article to be published in the newspaper, the Futurist, condemning some of the practices. Explain why you think the practices are unfair. You should not disclose your real name. Call yourself Marcel Nang.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 2 - Newspaper article (modèle, environ 260 mots)

**When Tradition Becomes an Excuse for Injustice**

*By Marcel Nang*

In many of our villages, certain practices towards women continue simply because "it has always been this way," never because anyone has stopped to ask whether they are fair. I have watched some of these practices closely in my own community, and I believe it is time we called them what they are: unjust.

Consider the custom by which a widow can be forced out of her late husband's house and property by his relatives, often within days of the funeral, regardless of how many years she spent building that home alongside him. She is left with nothing, while men who contributed far less to that household inherit everything simply because of their gender. This is not tradition; it is theft dressed up as custom.

Consider, too, how many young girls are still withdrawn from school earlier than their brothers, on the assumption that their future lies only in marriage and housework. A girl denied an education today becomes a woman with no independent means tomorrow, entirely dependent on a husband's goodwill for her survival, whatever he decides to do with that power.

These practices are rarely questioned, because those who benefit from them are also those who decide what counts as "normal." But normal is not the same as fair. A society that inherits injustice from its ancestors is still responsible for correcting it, not simply repeating it.

I do not write this to attack our culture, but to defend the women within it: our mothers, our sisters, our daughters, who deserve the same dignity and the same rights as any man in our villages.

**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of between 250 and 300 words on any one of the following topics. Make sure that you write in paragraphs.

**Topic 3.** You feel very strongly that some of the things happening in your school are wrong. Write a letter to your friend in another school in which you discuss what you do not like in your school. Your friend should be called Arouna and your name should be Nang Marcel. It will not be necessary to write the name of your school.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 3 - Personal letter (modèle, environ 230 mots)

Dear Arouna,

I hope this letter finds you well. I need to tell someone what has been bothering me at school lately, and I know I can trust you to understand, since you are not here to judge me for it.

Lately, I have noticed that some of our teachers punish students physically for the smallest mistakes, sometimes even for arriving a few minutes late because the only bus available was overcrowded. I do not think fear should be the main reason we behave well in class; it only teaches us to avoid getting caught, not to actually understand why something is wrong.

What troubles me even more is how unevenly the rules are applied. Students whose parents are close to the school administration seem to get away with things that would get anyone else suspended. It makes many of us feel like the rules exist only for those without connections, which is exactly the kind of unfairness a school should be teaching us to reject, not practising itself.

I have thought about speaking to the principal directly, but I am not sure how it would be received, since a student who complains is sometimes seen as a troublemaker rather than someone raising a fair concern.

Do things work this way at your school too, or is it just us? I would really like to know how you and your classmates handle situations like this, and whether you think it is worth raising with the administration here.

Write back soon and tell me how you are doing.

Your friend,
Nang Marcel

### Piège à éviter
La confusion de registre est l'erreur la plus fréquente sur cette section : rédiger le discours du sujet 1 avec un ton d'article de presse (trop démonstratif, destiné à un lectorat inconnu) ou rédiger la lettre du sujet 3 avec un ton trop formel, comme s'il s'agissait d'une lettre administrative, sont deux fautes régulièrement sanctionnées même quand le contenu est par ailleurs solide.

### Conseil
Avant de commencer à écrire le jour de l'examen, note en quelques mots au brouillon les éléments obligatoires du format choisi (pour une lettre personnelle : formule d'ouverture amicale, corps en 2-3 paragraphes, question ou nouvelle pour relancer l'échange, formule de clôture et signature) : cette liste de contrôle, relue juste avant de rendre la copie, évite d'oublier un élément qui coûte des points indépendamment de la qualité du contenu.
